description: Hello! I am participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge from Khulna. For this hackathon, I am working on the challenge "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!". My project focuses on analyzing NASA climate and weather datasets using Python and Streamlit to build an interactive coastal climate trend explorer for the Khulna and Sundarbans region. I am participating as a solo developer, ready to build an innovative earth observation dashboard.
summary: The Sundarbans & Coastal Climate Detective is an interactive climate trend analysis web application developed for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Using NASA POWER climate indicators, Python, Scikit-learn, and Streamlit, this dashboard visualizes historical temperature shifts (2010–2025), linear warming trends, and extreme rainfall variations across Bangladesh's coastal belt including Khulna, Satkhira, and Bagerhat. The tool helps researchers and local communities easily observe climate change patterns, extreme weather risks, and long-term temperature anomalies affecting the vulnerable Sundarbans ecosystem.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

The Sundarbans & Coastal Climate Detective is an interactive web application designed to analyze and visualize historical climate shifts and environmental trends in Bangladesh's coastal zone (focusing on Khulna, Satkhira, and Bagerhat). It fetches and processes authentic NASA POWER climate data, allowing users to explore long-term temperature anomalies (2010–2025) and annual rainfall variations through dynamic, real-time charts.

2. What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact?

The tool empowers local communities, researchers, and environmentalists to easily understand climate change patterns affecting the vulnerable Sundarbans ecosystem. By making complex earth observation data accessible and visually clear, it aids in assessing extreme weather risks and raising awareness about regional warming trends.

3. What tools, coding languages, or software did you use?

  • Programming Language: Python
  • Framework & UI: Streamlit for building the interactive web dashboard.
  • Data Processing & ML: Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn (Linear Regression for predictive trend analysis).
  • Visualization: Matplotlib for generating dynamic trend lines and precipitation bar charts.
  • Data Source: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) API.

4. How is your project creative?

It transforms raw, complex meteorological numbers into an intuitive, dark-themed dashboard tailored specifically for the Sundarbans coastal belt, bridging the gap between advanced NASA data science and local climate action.
